rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Judgements upon the fourth House
rules.meaning_historical_only: A new unnumbered substantive natal source section starts at original first-edition PDF603, separate from sibling number.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Concerning Parents ... Patrimony of the Father
rules.meaning_historical_only: The main original unnumbered source concerns father and patrimony/parental status; later mother chapter has its own separate heading.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: first, the fourth house
rules.meaning_historical_only: The fourth house itself is first in Lilly's hierarchy for the father and his circumstances.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: secondly, the Lord thereof
rules.meaning_historical_only: The fourth-house ruler is an additional and distinct father significator.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun in a diurnall Geniture
rules.meaning_historical_only: In daytime nativities the Sun is assigned father significator status; the birth sect must be known.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Saturn in a nocturnall
rules.meaning_historical_only: In nighttime nativities Saturn substitutes for Sun under this father-source selection; no unconditional same-luminary method.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Planet or Planets in the fourth
rules.meaning_historical_only: Any planet(s) occupying the fourth house form a fourth category of father indicators.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: these Significators or the most of them strong and fortunate
rules.meaning_historical_only: A favorable father assessment requires all or the majority of listed significators to be strong and fortunate.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: good aspect of Jupiter or Venus
rules.meaning_historical_only: Supportive aspect to Jupiter or Venus is another separate prerequisite or supporting testimony, not sufficient alone.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: happy condition of the Father after the Childs birth
rules.meaning_historical_only: The source claims favorable paternal condition after the child's birth, without actual family evidence.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Significators be unfortunate and impedited
rules.meaning_historical_only: Unfortunate and impeded significators are Lilly's explicit opposite branch.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: dejected and low condition ... many misfortunes
rules.meaning_historical_only: Under adverse testimony the source alleges low paternal status and misfortunes, not independently verified outcomes.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: some be strong and others weak
rules.meaning_historical_only: The mixed father indicators are not forced into either positive or negative extreme.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: they tend to a mediocrity
rules.meaning_historical_only: For mixed cases the author assigns a moderate result rather than certainty of prosperity or poverty.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: according to the nature of the Planet or Planets occupying fourth
rules.meaning_historical_only: In mixed configurations the original bases the parent's fortunes on planetary inhabitants of the fourth house.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if there be many therein
rules.meaning_historical_only: More than one planet in the fourth is expressly contemplated as a selection ambiguity.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: he that is most dignified preferred in judgment
rules.meaning_historical_only: Among multiple occupants the most dignified should be preferred rather than averaging all descriptions.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: best drawn from the Fathers own Nativity
rules.meaning_historical_only: Lilly states that evaluating the father from his OWN natal chart is preferable to the child's chart; different input requirements matter.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: fortunate Planets in fourth
rules.meaning_historical_only: Fortunate planets occupying fourth are a specified positive parental-fortune indicator.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: their Lords in angles or succedants
rules.meaning_historical_only: The rulers of those fortunate occupants must occupy angular or succedent houses for the favorable pattern.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: well disposed ... no aspect to the Infortunes
rules.meaning_historical_only: Favorable placement and absence of harsh malefic aspect are additional qualifications.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: condition of the Parents laudable and good
rules.meaning_historical_only: The author asserts favorable parental standing under the compound condition, not a measured life outcome.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Significators in cadent houses
rules.meaning_historical_only: Cadency of relevant parental significators is one of the asserted negative conditions.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: unfortunate starrs in the fourth
rules.meaning_historical_only: Unfortunate planets physically in fourth are listed as an additional adverse alternative.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Lords of the places ... afflicted of the Infortunes
rules.meaning_historical_only: Affliction of applicable house rulers by malefics forms a further alternative negative trigger.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Parents subject to many misfortunes
rules.meaning_historical_only: The source forecasts general parental difficulties on those sources, without calibrated probability.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: greatnesse ... by strength or debility of the Significators
rules.meaning_historical_only: Magnitude of the alleged good or bad fate should be graded by significator strength, with no numeric score given.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of the fourth in Reception with Lord of ascendant
rules.meaning_historical_only: Mutual reception of fourth ruler with the first ruler is one historical positive parent condition.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: or in Trine with him
rules.meaning_historical_only: Trine between the fourth and ascendant rulers is a separate positive alternative to reception.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: or Sextile with him
rules.meaning_historical_only: Sextile is another distinct positive alternative, not a required simultaneous trine.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: flourishing condition in the Father
rules.meaning_historical_only: Lilly claims these configurations indicate paternal flourishing, not a verified actual father life record.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun or Jupiter in fourth
rules.meaning_historical_only: A Sun or Jupiter occupant in fourth is said to indicate an esteemed father, using distinct alternatives.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Father to be a man of good quality
rules.meaning_historical_only: The author associates the fourth-house Sun/Jupiter condition with paternal standing rather than longevity.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Planet signifies Father be in angle or succedant
rules.meaning_historical_only: The father significator should occupy an angular or succedent house as part of the high-status branch.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: in his owne house or Exaltation
rules.meaning_historical_only: The same significator must additionally have domicile or exaltation dignity; otherwise result is not unconditional.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Father to be a man of esteeme and quality
rules.meaning_historical_only: The compound father-status condition alleges public esteem without human observations.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun Saturn Mars and Mercury in the fourth
rules.meaning_historical_only: Lilly prints a clustered list of planetary glyphs in fourth and states a short life; the scope of AND/OR is uncertain.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Father will live but a while
rules.meaning_historical_only: The author asserts a short paternal lifespan for that cluster, without a real-person survival timeline.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Jupiter and Venus by any application or aspect
rules.meaning_historical_only: Jupiter/Venus are named as additional source planets in a favorable father-longevity branch.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: in configuration with Sun or Saturn
rules.meaning_historical_only: The benefics' relations to Sun/Saturn as relevant father significators are included, under sect considerations.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: friendly aspect between them ... both strong
rules.meaning_historical_only: The planets must have a friendly aspect and both be strong in the favorable longevity branch.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: promise long life to the Father
rules.meaning_historical_only: Lilly claims paternal longevity under the combined testimony; no historical cases are verified.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun with North Node ... Moon in fourth
rules.meaning_historical_only: The source associates a particular Sun/node configuration and Moon in fourth with parental status; source glyph must be independently read.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Father to be of good Parents
rules.meaning_historical_only: One asserted result of the preceding combination is good paternal ancestry/standing.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Native not long lived
rules.meaning_historical_only: The same cluster assigns short life to the chart native, not the father; keep distinct persons and no validity claim.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun better dignified then Moon
rules.meaning_historical_only: The relative dignity of Sun and Moon is used to compare father/mother descent rather than predict absolute wealth.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Father better descended then the Mother
rules.meaning_historical_only: Lilly claims father from higher-status origins when Sun outranks Moon, not an observed social-class inference.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: and so the contrary
rules.meaning_historical_only: The opposite relative dignity is alleged to reverse the parental descent verdict; operator/tie rules unspecified.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun and Moon in [Mars glyph] masculine Signe
rules.meaning_historical_only: The exact original glyph and grammar in the masculine-sign parental outcome clause are uncertain; do not encode.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: shew dignity of the Father
rules.meaning_historical_only: The author attributes paternal dignity to the masculine-sign/luminary condition.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: short life to the Mother ... before the Father
rules.meaning_historical_only: The clause simultaneously makes a maternal earlier-death prediction; this remains source history, not medical evidence.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun or Lord of fourth peregrine in twelfth
rules.meaning_historical_only: Either Sun or fourth ruler peregrine in twelfth is alleged to predict low paternal condition.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Father of a very low condition
rules.meaning_historical_only: The preceding 12th-house configuration is linked to low paternal standing, an unsupported period social category.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun conjunct South Node and cadent
rules.meaning_historical_only: An adverse Sun/node combination with cadency is alleged to indicate poor parental standing; exact sign operator needs specialist check.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: in a Bestiall Signe
rules.meaning_historical_only: An additional sign-class requirement is specified in the adverse parental status branch.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: shewes abject Parents
rules.meaning_historical_only: The source asserts low parental social standing under the planetary combination, without human study.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun and Saturn in cadent houses and [Mars glyph]
rules.meaning_historical_only: Lilly adds an adverse Sun/Saturn configuration, with a glyph between conditions still uncertain.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: short life to the Father
rules.meaning_historical_only: The author alleges paternal short lifespan from Sun/Saturn conditions; no medical validation and no timeline.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Saturn infortuning Sun
rules.meaning_historical_only: An afflicting Saturn–Sun relationship forms an additional claimed death-cause source.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Father dyes of Melancholly
rules.meaning_historical_only: Lilly attributes paternal death to melancholy; this is not a medical diagnosis or causal evidence.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXXII Of the Mother
rules.meaning_historical_only: The next printed numbered chapter starts after horizontal divider on PDF604 and is substantive mother source to extract separately.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Mothers Significators ... tenth house
rules.meaning_historical_only: Only the opening of CXXII's indicator list is witnessed, not admitted as a fourth-house father condition.
